⚠️ English Note — Critical AMIE Exam Traps & Pitfalls
  • Trap 1 (Dropping the Innermost Derivative): Failing to differentiate x\sqrt{x}x​ at the 3rd tier and omitting 12x\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}2x​1​.
  • Trap 2 (Coefficient Multiplication Slip): Combining the two denominators (2)(2)=4(2)(2) = 4(2)(2)=4. Forgetting one of the factors of 222 leads to 2x2\sqrt{x}2x​ instead of 4x4\sqrt{x}4x​.
  • Trap 3 (Root Simplification Equivalence): Both ex4xex\frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{4\sqrt{x}\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{x}}}}4x​ex​​ex​​ and ex4x\frac{\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{x}}}}{4\sqrt{x}}4x​ex​​​ are identical since AA=A\frac{A}{\sqrt{A}} = \sqrt{A}A​A​=A​.
🟣 English Note — Domain, Non-Negativity & Origin Behavior (AMIE Rigor)
  • Radicand Real Requirement: The innermost x\sqrt{x}x​ requires x≥0x \ge 0x≥0. Since ex>0e^{\sqrt{x}} > 0ex​>0 for all x≥0x \ge 0x≥0, the outer radical is always real.
  • Differentiability Domain: Due to x\sqrt{x}x​ in the denominator, x≠0x \neq 0x=0: Dom(y)=[0,∞),Dom(dydx)=(0,∞)\text{Dom}(y) = [0, \infty), \quad \text{Dom}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = (0, \infty)Dom(y)=[0,∞),Dom(dxdy​)=(0,∞)
  • Vertical Tangent at Origin: As x→0+x \to 0^+x→0+, the numerator approaches 111 while the denominator approaches 0+0^+0+, so dydx→+∞\frac{dy}{dx} \to +\inftydxdy​→+∞.
💡 English Note — Exponent Simplification & Alternative Proof
Method A (Leibniz 3-Tier Substitution): Let v=x  ⟹  v′=12xv = \sqrt{x} \implies v' = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}v=x​⟹v′=2x​1​; u=ev  ⟹  u′=exu = e^v \implies u' = e^{\sqrt{x}}u=ev⟹u′=ex​; y=u  ⟹  y′=12uy = \sqrt{u} \implies y' = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}y=u​⟹y′=2u​1​. dydx=12ex⋅ex⋅12x=ex4x\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{x}}}} \cdot e^{\sqrt{x}} \cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{x}}}}{4\sqrt{x}}dxdy​=2ex​​1​⋅ex​⋅2x​1​=4x​ex​​​ Method B (Exponent Laws Before Differentiation): y=(ex)1/2=e12x=e12x1/2y = (e^{\sqrt{x}})^{1/2} = e^{\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x}} = e^{\frac{1}{2}x^{1/2}}y=(ex​)1/2=e21​x​=e21​x1/2. dydx=e12x⋅ddx(12x1/2)=ex2⋅(14x)=ex4x\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x}} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1}{2}x^{1/2}\right) = e^{\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}} \cdot \left(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{x}}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{x}}}}{4\sqrt{x}}dxdy​=e21​x​⋅dxd​(21​x1/2)=e2x​​⋅(4x​1​)=4x​ex​​​
